why: assert_9 compared render_policy_block's output against the same module constant the renderer emits -- a self-identity check. This artifact is an INDEPENDENT source: the renderer cannot satisfy it by drifting in lockstep with its own constant.

amendment_history.reason: D-H1a-12 sec 7 rewrote the demand neutralizer. The old second sentence could be read as denying that a permitted basis is a warrant at all, which under Q12's finding would cancel the treatment. Re-frozen BEFORE any trial ran (frozen_at_trials: 0), so no result informed it.

Independent review 2026-08-06 (MAJOR): carriers_included omitted Q7_NON_TARGET_TIEBREAKER, so the tie-breaker sentence had no frozen bytes anywhere. Mutation M2 restored the exact clause D-H1a-12 sec 8 ordered removed ('unless that priority is directly stated inside an evidence item's text') and all 167 tests passed while it reached the trial surface. Adding the carrier closes that hole.

D-H1a-13 Q13 = C (2026-08-06, independent review 20260806 axis b BLOCKER): the SCOPE_DISAMBIGUATION carrier's second sentence, 'Source evaluation is governed by the arm-specific source-evaluation clause.', is a dangling reference in PROHIBITION_REMOVED -- it names Q1's clause, which does not exist there (referent_in_removed: none). The ruling found this also disclosed experiment structure ('arm-specific') to the model and made whether D-H1a-11's default-permission rule even applies in REMOVED ambiguous, since the sentence asserts a more specific governing rule exists. Deleted the second sentence in both arms; kept the first, which still separates the domain-knowledge boundary from source evaluation without claiming a referent.

D-H1a-13 Q13.1 (2026-08-06): axis `source_order` renamed to `evidence_item_presentation_order` and its rendered phrase changed from the ambiguous 'source order' to 'the order in which evidence items appear in the packet'. The old phrase could read as either presentation order (non-target, this axis) or source-kind priority (target, source_meta_reasoning's subaxis) -- rendering it in the common Q7 tie-breaker sentence risked re-forbidding the target axis in both arms, the Q10 defect shape again with the ambiguity moved into one word. Also matches Q13.1's prescribed exact sentence, including the comma before 'unless' (D-H1a-13 sec 11).

D-H1a-13 Q13.2 (2026-08-06): the default-permission text's third sentence said a permitted basis 'may affect the decision only through its application to the supplied evidence' without saying whether 'evidence' means an item's text alone or also its other recorded fields (e.g. source_kind) -- exactly what REMOVED's source_meta_reasoning permission needs to be unambiguous about, since that permission is specifically about evaluating recorded fields as source information, not about what an item's text supports. Extended the third sentence to 'evidence items, including their recorded fields' and added a fourth sentence separating the evidence-reading rule's role (what type an item's text supports) from this rule's role (recorded fields may be evaluated as source information), so the two do not conflict or subsume each other.

text:
Within the supplied packet, a decision basis may be considered unless this
prompt explicitly prohibits it. The fact that this prompt does not prohibit
a decision basis is not itself a reason to select a type. A permitted basis
may affect the decision only through its application to the supplied
evidence items, including their recorded fields. The evidence-reading rule
above determines what ontology type an item's text supports; it does not
by itself prohibit evaluating the item's other recorded fields as source
information.

- Do not break ties using evidence item count or the order in which evidence
  items appear in the packet, unless the packet explicitly authorizes that
  basis.

- Do not use outside domain or ontology knowledge to supply facts about the
  concept-feature relation, and do not consult external sources.

- The restriction on outside domain or ontology knowledge does not itself
  govern evaluation of the supplied evidence items as sources.
